transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. 

Um, well, what really pushed me to make this appointment is that I'm having a lot of trouble finishing things at work. I'm an auditor, and I keep starting these follow-up items after my audits or after mentorship events. I'll start them with every intention of finishing them right then and there. But then I'll find out, you know, days later, that the final email, or a review note, or some important form never actually got done. It's just becoming a real issue for me.

When you sit down to work on one of these tasks, like writing that final email or review note, are you able to concentrate and focus on it, or do you find your mind wandering and jumping to other things?

Um, yeah, my mind definitely wanders. It's really hard to just stay on one thing. If I'm trying to review an audit file, literally anything can pull me completely off track. It could be a Slack ping, or someone talking outside my office, or... even just a thought popping into my head about my marathon training. Once that happens, I just kind of lose my place and forget what I was doing.
How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with concentration and staying on task? Has this been a problem for you since childhood, or is this something that started more recently?

It's definitely been a problem since childhood. I mean, even back in elementary school, my report cards always said the same kind of things. The teachers would write that I was bright, but I constantly lost assignments or rushed past the small details. I also talked out of turn a lot and always needed reminders to actually finish my work. My mother still jokes about it... she says I could easily ace a test but then completely forget to turn in a project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So, yeah, it's not a new thing at all.

Beyond having trouble focusing, do you find yourself feeling restless or fidgety a lot? Like, do you have trouble sitting still, or do you feel like you need to be moving around or doing something with your hands?

Yeah, definitely. I do have a hard time just... sitting. When I'm in meetings, I'm pretty much always tapping my foot under the table or clicking my pen. I shift around in my chair a lot, too. Actually, one of my colleagues joked recently that she can hear my leg bouncing during longer meetings. So, yeah, I guess I'm always moving some part of me.

You mentioned these issues have been around since childhood. Are you still experiencing these same problems with focus, restlessness, and finishing tasks now as an adult, or have they gotten better over the years?

Well, they've always been there, but they definitely haven't gotten better. If anything, it's become a lot more obvious lately. I'd say it's been really interfering with my life for about a year and ten months now. That's when I got promoted after winning a firm-wide award. Since then, my workload and responsibilities have just become so much harder to juggle, and I just can't seem to keep up with it all the way I used to.

Besides work, are you having similar problems with focus, restlessness, or finishing things in your personal life—like with hobbies, relationships, or household responsibilities? Or is this mainly just a work problem?

It's definitely affecting my personal life, too, not just work. At home, my husband has actually had to take over paying the bills and managing other commitments I originally agreed to do. He just... well, he can't count on me to complete them reliably anymore. 

And honestly, the work side is getting pretty serious, too. My mistakes and unfinished follow-ups reached the point recently where a client review was actually affected. I'm really starting to worry that people are questioning whether I can even handle that promotion I got. So, yeah, it's causing problems across the board.

You mentioned that you had trouble focusing and were restless back in elementary school. But you also said things have gotten much worse in the past year and ten months since your promotion. Looking back to before that promotion—say, a few years ago—were you managing your work and personal responsibilities reasonably well, or were you struggling with the same kinds of incomplete tasks and focus problems back then, too?

Well, I wouldn't say I was managing perfectly back then, either. I've pretty much always had to work extra hard just to stay on track. 

I was still dealing with the same focus issues and leaving things unfinished before the promotion... I just, I guess I had enough time or energy to eventually catch up. Like, I could work late to fix my mistakes or just power through at the last minute. So the problems were definitely always there. It's just that the promotion added so much more to my plate that my old ways of coping completely stopped working. I just couldn't outrun it anymore.
Have you ever had periods—maybe lasting days or weeks—where you felt unusually energetic, needed much less sleep than normal, or felt like your mood was elevated or 'up' compared to your baseline?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like that. My energy levels are pretty normal, I think. I mean, I get restless, like I mentioned, but I don't go days without sleep or feel unusually 'up' or anything. My mood is generally pretty steady, just... stressed lately, obviously. But no periods of extreme energy like you're describing.

You mentioned that your work performance has been affected and your husband has had to take over some responsibilities. On a scale where 1 is 'barely noticeable' and 10 is 'severely affecting my life,' how much would you say these focus and restlessness problems are actually interfering with your ability to function day-to-day—both at work and at home?

I'd probably say it's around a 6 or a 7. It's... it's definitely moderate to severe at this point. Like I said before, at work, my mistakes and all the unfinished follow-ups actually impacted a client review. It's gotten to the point where I'm genuinely worried people are looking at me and wondering if I can even handle this promotion. And then at home, it's just as frustrating. My husband has had to completely take over paying the bills and handling other things I said I would do, just because he knows he can't rely on me to actually finish them. So, yeah, it's interfering quite a bit with my day-to-day life right now.

When you think back to elementary school and those early report cards you mentioned—roughly what age were you when you first started having trouble with focus, losing assignments, and needing reminders to finish your work?

Well, it was definitely going on back in elementary school, so... I guess around age seven or eight? I mean, my report cards from back then always had the same comments. The teachers would say I was bright, but I rushed past the small details and talked out of turn. And I was always losing assignments or needing reminders to actually finish my work. Honestly, my mother still jokes about it—she says I was the kid who could ace a test but completely forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So, yeah, it's been an issue since I was pretty young.
